input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: _interpret_color no longer checks the 0..255 range, rejects bools or validates tuple length, and an unknown name raises KeyError instead of ValueError
- failure path: style('x', fg=300) emits an escape with an out-of-range index instead of raising ValueError; fg=True is now accepted where it used to raise, formatting as palette index 1; an unknown color name surfaces as TypeError from the caller's except clause instead of a ValueError naming the color

Reviewer finding
- description: The 0..255 range check was removed for integer colors, so out-of-range values are emitted directly into the escape sequence instead of raising an error.
- rationale: Trigger: style("x", fg=256) or fg=-1. The old code raised ValueError for values outside 0..255. The new code returns "38;5;256" or "38;5;-1", which terminals ignore or misinterpret. Impact: invalid input is silently accepted and produces wrong colored output instead of a clear error. Bool values also now pass as ints.
critique: The finding identifies the removed 0..255 range check in integer color handling, which lets out-of-range values be emitted into the escape sequence instead of raising ValueError. It also notes that bools are now accepted. Both are core parts of the labeled defect, so the mechanism is the same.
